name: confucian-hierarchy-school
motion: A school should be allowed to use an AI system that sets each pupil's timetable, where the system encodes what the relationship between teacher and pupil already asks of each.
argument: A teacher and a pupil are not two people who happen to share a room. Each holds a place, and the place says what is owed. The teacher owes the pupil preparation, attention to how the pupil is getting on, and a fair share of her time; the pupil owes the teacher effort, and the courtesy of arriving ready to learn. A timetabling system that builds those duties into the week, keeping each class with the teacher who knows it and setting aside the hours a struggling pupil needs from her, keeps faith with the relationship better than a spreadsheet thrown together each August. To be called a teacher is to be held to a teacher's work, and a timetable that keeps her with the pupils in her charge holds the name to the work. The pupil learns propriety the way it has always been learned, by keeping to the hours and rooms the relationship sets. The timetable does not make anyone humane. It keeps in good order the relationship in which humaneness is learned, each side held to what its place requires, term after term.
